rounds.reply:
It looks like the issue is that Three.js is not being loaded correctly. The browser console is showing a `ReferenceError: THREE is not defined`, which means that the Three.js library is not being loaded into the global scope.

To fix this, we need to ensure that the Three.js script is loaded before the `engine.js` script. We can do this by moving the Three.js script tag before the `engine.js` script tag in the `index.html` file.

Here is the updated `index.html` file:

```index.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Minecraft Voxel Engine</title>
    <style>
        body { margin: 0; }
        canvas { display: block; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js"></script>
    <script type="module" src="engine.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

After making this change, the Three.js library should be loaded before the `engine.js` script, and the `THREE` object should be available in the global scope. This should resolve the `ReferenceError: THREE is not defined` error and allow the voxel engine to run correctly.
